claims.text: Incorporating MoS2 into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix will reduce its coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Incorporating MoS2 into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix will reduce its wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
MoS2 incorporated into the matrix will form a lubricating tribofilm during sliding.
The MoS2-derived tribofilm provides a low-shear-strength contact layer.
The tribofilm is thermally stable throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C test regime.
The tribofilm can adapt to temperature changes while maintaining its lubricating properties.
MoS2 can oxidize at high temperatures.
It is uncertain whether MoS2 will retain its lubricating properties at 800 °C in air.
The modified material is predicted to have lower friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi under identical sliding conditions across the entire temperature range.
The modified material is predicted to have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi under identical sliding conditions across the entire temperature range.
The proposed performance boundary is sliding in air from room temperature to 800 °C under loads typical of sliding-wear tests.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that the MoS2-derived tribofilm is thermally stable and maintains lubrication across the full regime, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that MoS2 may oxidize and may not retain lubrication at 800 °C in air.
The hypothesis and predicted outcome categorically claim lower friction and wear across the entire range through 800 °C, while the uncertainty field questions performance at the upper limit.
